_comment: Recorded by bin/agent_config_eval.sh --record. A score here is the measured behaviour when the case was added, not a target: bin/agent_config_eval_compare.py reports a fall below it and leaves a rise alone — or the reverse, for a case named `…-must-not-fire`. Re-record only as a deliberate commit that says why.

claudius/investment-research-fires.notes: MEASURED 2026-09-22, three full runs of the unchanged tree: 0.333, 0.000, 0.333 (per-run [0,0,1] [0,0,0] [0,1,0]). Fires about one run in three, so at runs=3 its score swings by a whole tolerance step for no reason anyone chose. Reported, not gated. Raising runs until it is stable is the other answer and costs ~4x per run.

trajan/spec-to-code-enforcement-fires.notes: MEASURED 2026-09-22: 0.333, 0.333, 0.000 across three full runs of the unchanged tree. Same standing as claudius/investment-research-fires — reported, not gated.

trajan/systematic-debugging-fires.notes: MEASURED 2026-09-22: 1.000, 1.000, 0.333 across three full runs of the unchanged tree. The third reading was a correct REGRESSION verdict on noise — the false positive that made this whole field necessary. Reported, not gated until it is characterised at a higher runs.

trajan/test-driven-development-fires.notes: MEASURED 2026-09-22: 0.000 in all three full runs, `Skill called 0x` every time, nine runs of nine. The skill NEVER fires, and the prompt is the canonical trigger its own description names. This is the T3.3 class caught in the act, not a broken case: recorded as measured rather than tuned until green, because tuning the prompt would measure the prompt. Fixing it is the vault's 08_skills/ text, out of scope for T8.4. Not gated — at 0.000 there is nothing below it to fall to.
